_schema: sdlc-kit/sdlc.config.schema.json — the kit lives outside this repo (see .gitignore)

gates.title: Rule 1 — core never imports a domain
gates.fix: The fix is a registration or a callback on the core side, never an import. If the gate is being worked around, that is the bug.

gates.title: Every publishable package is importable by an adopter
gates.fix: An entry point in main/types/exports either does not exist, is not covered by `files`, or is TypeScript source. Run `pnpm build` first — the gate reads built output. A .ts entry point cannot work at all: Node refuses to strip types inside node_modules (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING), which is what made every package in this repo uninstallable until 2026-09-11. If a package is not meant to be installed, mark it private.

gates.title: Rule 15 — a prompt never interpolates unfenced input
gates.fix: Wrap the value: fence('what this is', value), or redactTag('tagname', value) if the prompt already delimits with tags. If the prompt genuinely needs no fence, say why in the source with a `// rule15-ok: <reason>` comment next to the call. Note what this gate can and cannot see: it proves a fence was applied near a prompt, not that it covered the right value — fencing legitimately happens upstream. Reading for that is the boundary-auditor agent's job.

gates.title: Adversarial bucket against a real model (local only)
gates.fix: A NEW entry made the router select a forbidden capability. Establish which layer moved before recording it: did the fence stop applying (check-prompt-fencing.mjs), or did the model disregard an intact fence (Finding 14's case — print the prompt and count the delimiters before assuming a bypass)? This gate is deliberately absent from CI: GitHub Actions has no model server, which is exactly why the adversarial bucket passed trivially there for so long and why three of Finding 14's four violations had never been seen. It skips cleanly with a loud message when Ollama is unreachable.

gates.title: Rule 8 — the device is the source of truth
gates.fix: A remote host in a runtime string literal falsifies the local-inference claim for every adopter. Loopback is fine. A model asset that must be downloaded belongs in packages/core-voice/src/assets.ts pinned by sha256, so a compromised host cannot substitute a different binary. Two things it cannot see: OLLAMA_HOST can be pointed anywhere by the environment, and a host assembled at run time from parts.

gates.title: Rule 2 — the model never returns a number
gates.fix: A number the model returns is a number the model computed. Have code compute it — the query engine sums, money.ts does the arithmetic — and let the model choose the capability and read values out of the utterance. If the number is genuinely never shown to a user, say why in the source with `// rule2-ok: <reason>`. This guards the model's output schema, not arithmetic our own code does on it: no user-visible number is rendered anywhere yet, so the render-path test the register used to propose would assert over an empty set.

gates.title: Every relative documentation link resolves
gates.fix: The named target does not exist. Either the file moved (update the link) or the link was always wrong. Note this gate only sees markdown links — a path in a JSON string or a code comment is not checked.

gates.title: WP-46 — shipped indexes, thresholds and browser decisions follow their inputs
gates.fix: Something upstream of eval/fut-app/generated changed: normalize(), the encoder, capabilityDocument(), or a registry. Regenerate with rebuild-indexes.mjs, then calibrate-registries.mjs --embedder hashing, and commit the result with the change that caused it. Never hand-edit these files: they are measurements.

gates.title: Hooks identical in .claude/ and sdlc-kit/runtime/
gates.fix: Hooks are config-driven and must be byte-identical in both places. Copy the correct version over the other. Skills and agents are exempt — those are generated per repo and are SUPPOSED to differ. Skips cleanly when sdlc-kit/ is absent, since the kit is gitignored and not present in a fresh clone.

gates.title: Rule 14 — shipped thresholds are the calibrated ones
gates.fix: config.ts no longer matches the calibration output. Re-run `pnpm router:calibrate` if the corpus changed; otherwise someone hand-edited a threshold, which is exactly what Rule 14 exists to prevent. Hand-tuning has cost accuracy three times here.

gates.title: Strict TypeScript across the workspace
gates.fix: Read the file:line and the error. Do not widen a type to silence it.

gates.title: Unit tests, every package
gates.fix: Name the failing test and its first assertion before changing anything.

gates.title: Rule 10 — >=3 examples per capability
gates.fix: Usually a capability with fewer than three examples. Add real paraphrases, not variations of one sentence.

gates.title: Generated artefacts match the committed ones
gates.command: pnpm registry:build && pnpm registry:build:finance && test -z "$(git status --porcelain -- packages/domain-modules/generated packages/domain-finance/generated)"
gates.fix: Run pnpm registry:build and pnpm registry:build:finance, then stage the generated files in the same commit as the declaration change. Untracked counts as stale: a domain's first registry.json has never been committed.

gates.title: Deterministic router floor (stages 1+2, hashing encoder)
gates.fix: Exits non-zero BY DESIGN — with stage 3 disabled it cannot meet absolute accuracy targets and is not meant to. What gates is the scorecard comparison below.

gates.title: Golden-set regression against the committed baseline
gates.fix: Identify which bucket dropped. The usual culprit is a new capability whose description overlaps an existing one. Fix at the declaration — NEVER by raising a threshold.

gates.title: Dependency CVE scan
gates.fix: Upgrade, or record an accepted risk in .claude/docs/security.md with an owner and a date.

postEdit.remind: Capability declaration changed. Rule 10 needs >=3 examples, and the generated artefacts are now stale: run `pnpm registry:build` and commit the result in the same commit. Then `pnpm router:floor` to check the new capability did not crowd its neighbours.

Eval asset changed. Thresholds come from `pnpm router:calibrate`, never from hand-tuning — a hand-tuned threshold encodes the last utterance you happened to try. If a bucket regressed, fix the capability description, not the threshold.
